In the following weeks, dysphagia worsened, and he developed focal myoclonus and discrete appendicular ataxia in the left hemicorpus, diplopia, and alternating horizontal nystagmus.

Due to respiratory failure with apneas, he required intubation and mechanical ventilation.

extractions.quote:
A previously healthy 60-year-old man presented with a 1-week history of mild dizziness and swallowing difficulties.

In the following weeks, dysphagia worsened, and he developed focal myoclonus and discrete appendicular ataxia in the left hemicorpus, diplopia, and alternating horizontal nystagmus.

He appeared anxious.

Due to respiratory failure with apneas, he required intubation and mechanical ventilation.

Routine hematological and biochemical testing, and brain MRI were normal. CSF analysis showed three oligoclonal bands without corresponding bands in serum. There was no malignancy on whole-body F-18-fluorodeoxyglucose PET.

Upper gastrointestinal series confirmed a severely disturbed swallowing act.

Onconeural antibodies (Hu, Ri, Yo, CV2, Ma1, Ma2, Amphiphysine, SOX, Zic, Gad65, Tr, ANNA3, and PCA) and autoimmune antibodies to neuronal cell-surface and synaptic proteins (AMPAR, CASPR2, DPPX, GABAbR, m GluR1, m GluR5, GlyR, LGI1, and NMDAR) were negative in serum. GlyR-ab were, however, detected in CSF. A second serum sample was weakly positive for GlyR-ab.
